specAmbiguitiesResolved: An order/job is the fulfillment projection of exactly one M09 commercial intent (PURCHASE -> purchase order, SERVICE_BOOKING -> service job); PAID_CONTACT/PAID_LOOKUP are not orders.

Order REQUESTED means requested by UptimeBuyer (created with the CREATED intent); transport/egress truth stays on the intent/attempt axes, so nothing fabricates REQUESTED on the external-outcome axis.

Broker mirror: SUBMITTED/CONFIRMED/REFUNDED/REVERSED -> order ACCEPTED (provider acceptance only, never ORDERED/fulfilled); UNKNOWN -> UNKNOWN; FAILED -> CANCELLED (cancellation requested), REJECTED (after an attempt) or FAILED, with the no-effect stamp.

Material changes include a routine update whose quantity, price/currency or ETA is worse than the approved terms (approved terms = candidate quantity, intent max, plan action recovery ETA); equal or better terms are not material.

A pre-egress revocation is definite no effect: it does not invalidate the plan or move the incident, so a fresh approval can create the INV-07 linked successor; a post-egress revocation blocks, invalidates the executing plan (in-flight) and escalates.
VERIFIED/DISPUTED are operator outcomes (receiving inspection / work verification), never provider words; a blocked order cannot be VERIFIED.
Incident VERIFYING is driven when every live order/job of the plan reports completion; plan COMPLETED when every one is VERIFIED and its payment is CONFIRMED/REFUNDED/REVERSED. RECOVERED stays M11's.
Fulfillment webhooks for broker-paid accounts are verified in M10 with webhook_verifier_ref only (ADR 0005); superseded verifiers stay valid 30 days, only for orders pinned to that revision.
Polling needs a separately provisioned status credential; the paid credential_ref is never resolved outside the broker (HTTPS adapter is UNSUPPORTED without one).
securityReview: Webhook forgery/replay: constant-time HMAC over timestamp + raw bytes, 300 s window both directions, >= 32-byte keys, strict schema (no URL/tenant/revision), 64 KiB cap before any lookup, replay key (tenant, account, event id), observation dedupe by namespaced event key; INVALID deliveries recorded without occupying the replay key (M02 design).
Stale-revision retargeting: target must be pinned to the verifying revision (quarantine REVISION_MISMATCH) and the observation FK pins the order's revision in the database.

SSRF: polling targets only from the pinned revision; HTTPS adapter path from validated tokens, endpoint policy bound by digest, M07 guarded transport (no private/metadata addresses, no redirects); webhook bodies cannot carry URLs.
IDOR/cross-tenant: binding-derived tenant; every read/command resolves ids inside the caller tenant with uniform RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE; foreign worker sweeps see nothing (T-010).
Races: one lock order (planning -> authority -> intent -> order, FOR NO KEY UPDATE) shared with the M09 linearization; polling claims SKIP LOCKED; concurrent request/dispatch/poll/revoke tested.

unresolvedRisks: No real merchant/technician webhook, status endpoint, order or payment has run; vendor raw-status vocabularies are illustrative and must be mapped per real provider adapter.
Superseded webhook verifiers remain valid for 30 days for orders pinned to them; a leaked old verifier can forge fulfillment observations for those orders until then (never payment).
Invalid webhook deliveries are recorded (unauthenticated write amplification without an edge rate limit), as in M07.
Raw webhook bodies are stored in fulfillment_observations (and transiently in job payloads) without a retention/erasure worker; they may contain personal data (FR-23 retention is M13/M02).
Scheduling (runFulfillmentObservationJobs, pollFulfillmentStatus, the two outbox consumers, syncIncidentForOrder) must be wired by the deployment (M14); nothing runs on a timer.
Provider-side cancellation after egress is UNSUPPORTED: the operator gets a blocked order with a cancellation request and must cancel with the provider out of band.
